quote: and it is crazy in my house. Can we talk on Monday?
stewart_read: This is a reschedule request rather than the scripted 'how long will this take' time-constraint objection, so the schema fit is loose — it's better read as an unlisted reschedule-deflection pattern. The rep's response (compress to 5 minutes rather than accept a vague future callback) is the right instinct even without a scripted template for it.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as a hard timing objection requiring a firm anchor per protocols.time_constraint, but the customer's language is about her house being chaotic right now, not about call length.
coaching_implication: Praise this improvisation specifically — the rep avoided a soft callback by negotiating time-boxed value in the moment. Worth naming explicitly as a repeatable move.

quote: I'm seeing here you just put in a request to get some more information on solar for your home. Is that correct?
stewart_read: The rep never actually asks what interested her in solar — he references the form and moves straight into rescheduling logistics once she interrupts. The emotional anchor (verify.interest_in_solar) is skipped entirely and never recovered later in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be strategic time-compression given her stated crisis, but the whole rest of the call proceeds through verify items at normal pace, so there's no evidence the rep deliberately dropped this one for time — it was just never returned to.
coaching_implication: Flag as a missed anchor: even one sentence ('what's got you looking into solar?') would have given the rep something to tie the Monday visit to instead of a bare logistics booking.

quote: Well, the garages are connected, so I don't know. Not the houses. Just the Oh, okay. Garage.
stewart_read: The home-type answer is ambiguous (shared garage, unclear if it's a townhome) and the rep just says 'Cool' and moves on without clarifying what this means for roof/solar feasibility on a shared structure.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged it immaterial to qualification since she confirmed sole ownership and a separate power meter — a defensible reactive skip, not a strategic one.
coaching_implication: Note for the closer: home structure (attached garages) is unresolved and should be clarified on the roof/design call.

quote: No. I don't think so. That's why I was getting ready to just go on and buy the system because I don't charge a lot of anything.
stewart_read: This is not a cost objection — she's confused about her own credit number and anxious that it may disqualify her, while stating she has cash and good card history. Per Spencer's operator note in qualifiers.credit_qualifier, stated credit often differs from pulled credit, and the rep never reassures her that the actual number will be verified by the closer rather than her self-report.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as a cost/affordability objection since she offers a cash deal alternative, but her own words frame it purely around the credit-score number and confusion about why it's low, not about price.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to say plainly that the stated number isn't the final word — the actual credit pull happens later — rather than letting her sit in confusion and pivot the conversation himself to 'cash deal.'

quote: Yeah. And can I purchase it in three payments, or does it have to be all at once? Those kinds of questions I need answers to.
stewart_read: The customer directly asks a financing-structure question; rather than answering (which would be scope creep) or clearly bridging to the specialist, the rep gives a vague 'we'll send someone by to give you the cost' — a soft deflection rather than the clean escape hatch language the schema recommends.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have intentionally avoided answering because it's genuinely closer-tier content — the correct instinct — but the delivery is mumbled and non-committal rather than a confident bridge.
coaching_implication: Model the clean bridge line: 'That's exactly what our specialist will walk through with you Monday' — same non-answer, delivered with more confidence and specificity so the customer isn't left hanging.

quote: So I don't know what you guys would charge me. No. I think the credit score is around 611.
stewart_read: Buried inside the credit confusion is a strong buying signal — she says she was 'getting ready to just go on and buy the system' outright and has cash on hand. This is a highly motivated, cash-capable customer, not a hesitant one.
coaching_implication: The rep should have anchored on 'you were already planning to buy this outright' as a forward-pulling hook when booking Monday's visit, instead of letting it pass as background noise to the credit tangent.
